item.title: Russell Brand Sentenced to 10½ Years in Jail for Rape and Sexual Assault
item.description: A jury had found the U.K. actor guilty of one count of rape and three counts of sexual assault, following a four-week trial.

item.title: Nvidia Stock Slides After Chip Maker Opens Probe
item.description: Stocks advanced, with the Dow gaining more than 600 points, while Nvidia’s shares fell after the company launched an investigation into Chief Executive Officer Jensen Huang.

item.title: The Chinese Woman at the Center of a Spy Probe After an Affair With Jensen Huang
item.description: Alice Huang went from journalism to finance, then met the Nvidia CEO as executive of Megaspeed, a provider of computing power.

item.title: Best High-Yield Savings Accounts of November 2026: Up to 5.00%
item.description: Beat average interest rates with one of these top high-yield savings accounts.

item.title: Oil Slides More Than 3% as Trump Downplays Prospect of New Iran Strikes
item.description: Trump said in an interview with CNN Sunday that further strikes on Iran were highly unlikely as long as negotiations over Tehran’s nuclear program and the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz made progress.

item.title: Nvidia’s Board Investigates Reports That CEO Was Spying Target After Affair
item.description: Jensen Huang apologized for being unfaithful to his wife, after he had an affair with an executive suspected of working for Chinese intelligence.

item.title: What to Know About Nvidia’s Investigation After CEO’s Affair
item.description: The board is looking into whether secrets were shared during Jensen Huang’s relationship with an executive suspected of working for Chinese intelligence.

item.title: Jensen Huang Apologized to Nvidia for His Infidelity. His Kids Are on Staff.
item.description: The Nvidia CEO has elevated his children to prominence. His board is investigating reports that he was an espionage target.

item.title: China’s Push for Influence in the South Pacific Is Running Into Resistance
item.description: Washington is enjoying a boost in the region’s strategic islands as political winds shift and Australia pursues aggressive diplomacy.

item.title: The New Political Era: Less Party Loyalty, Big Election Swings
item.description: The midterms were the latest vote to show elections from the U.S. to Europe are getting more volatile.

item.title: These Maps Show the Gangs and Guerrillas Ruling More Than 200 Million People
item.description: Cartels, crime syndicates and rebel groups run shadow states across 60 nations, sidelining weak governments and moving billions of dollars beyond the reach of law enforcement.

item.title: A Missionary Pope Faces a Chain Saw-Wielding Populist in Argentina
item.description: Pope Leo’s message of compassion for the poor clashes with Javier Milei’s radical economic overhaul, symbolized by his trademark chain saw.

item.title: Party That Defeated Apartheid Hits Electoral Setback in South Africa
item.description: Final results for local elections tallied Sunday showed the worst result on record for the African National Congress, which won just 31% of the votes cast.

item.title: Netanyahu Rival Gets First Run at Power, but Hurdles Lie in Wait
item.description: Gadi Eisenkot must overcome disagreements among political parties to assemble a coalition robust enough to replace Israel’s longest-serving leader, Benjamin Netanyahu.

item.title: Iconic Saudi Tower Hit as Yemen’s Houthis Target Riyadh
item.description: Officials acknowledged damage to the building after the Iran-backed rebels mounted their latest attack on the capital.

item.title: Do You Know England’s Founding Father? It’s OK, England Doesn’t Either.
item.description: Next year marks 1,100 years since England named its first king. Celebrations face one major hurdle: Hardly anyone knows who Æthelstan is.

item.title: The Growing Push to Protect Trophy Hunting in Africa
item.description: Western animal-rights groups are pushing to ban hunting-trophy imports, but are facing opposition from African countries renowned for protecting wildlife.

item.title: Six Dead in Shooting at Market Square in Poland
item.description: Three others were found dead in the home of the suspect, who is in custody; an official calls it a terrorist attack .

item.title: New Zealand’s Conservatives Narrowly Lead in Election
item.description: Prime Minister Christopher Luxon and allies face weeks of uncertainty as late ballots are tallied.

item.title: Someone Is Causing Chaos Across Europe. The Question Is: Who?
item.description: Authorities are scrambling to figure out the source of a series of bomb threats and hacks that diverted aircraft and led to the evacuation of media outlets.
